hook.line: Sometimes the honest answer is "it's your call". Spanish hands the decision back by repeating the verb: if you want it, do it.
hook.en: If you want to invite her, invite her. (to a friend)

examples.en: If you want to buy it, buy it. (to a friend)

examples.es: Si quiere ir, que vaya; a mí me da igual.
examples.en: If he wants to go, let him go; I don't mind.

examples.es: Si quiere decírselo, que se lo diga.
examples.en: If she wants to tell him, let her tell him.
If you want to come, come. (to a friend)

examples.es: Si Hernando quiere pagar, que pague.
examples.en: If Hernando wants to pay, let him pay.

examples.es: Si quiere cambiar el menú, que lo cambie.
examples.en: If she wants to change the menu, let her change it.

rule:
To say "do what you like, I won't stop you", Spanish repeats the verb.

To the person: *si quieres* + a plain command. *Si quieres venir, ven.*
About someone else: *si quiere* + *que* + the wish form. *Si quiere ir, que vaya.*

Pronouns go before the verb after *que*: *que se lo diga*.

It hands the decision back, so it can sound cold. Add *a mí me da igual* only if you truly do not mind.
smallPrint: Teachers call *que vaya* an indirect command: a wish aimed at a third person.

options: If he wants to go, let him go.
If he went, he should have stayed.
If I go, he can go too.
If you buy it, I'll buy it too.
If you want to buy it, buy it.
You'd better not buy it.

options: If Hernando paid, he should pay.
Hernando wants me to pay.
If Hernando wants to pay, let him pay.

readAndPick.es: Si quiere decírselo, que se lo diga.
options: If she wants to tell him, let her tell him.
If she told him, she should tell me.
She wants me to tell him.
If you come, I'll leave.
If you want to come, come.
If I come, you come.

readAndPick.es: Si quiere irse, que se vaya; a mí me da igual.
options: If he leaves, I'll be sad.
He wants to leave, and I mind a lot.
If he wants to leave, let him; I don't mind.
If you want to call her, call her.
If you call her, she will answer.

If she wants to change the menu, let her change it.

yourTurn.prompt: Talking to a friend. Choose *cómpratelo* or *que se lo compre*: Si quieres comprártelo, ___. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: To the person you are talking to, use the plain command.

yourTurn.prompt: About Hernando. Choose *paga* or *que pague*: Si Hernando quiere pagar, ___. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Si Hernando quiere pagar, que pague.
yourTurn.why: About someone else, use *que* + the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: If you want to come, come. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: A friend is *tú*, so *si quieres* and the plain command.

yourTurn.prompt: If she wants to tell him, let her tell him.
yourTurn.answer: Si quiere decírselo, que se lo diga.
accept: Si ella quiere decírselo, que se lo diga.
yourTurn.why: About her, so *que* + *diga*, with the pronouns before the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: If he wants to go, let him go; I don't mind.
yourTurn.answer: Si quiere ir, que vaya; a mí me da igual.
accept: Si él quiere ir, que vaya; a mí me da igual.
yourTurn.why: *A mí me da igual* says you really don't mind.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Vale: *Si quieres cambiar el menú, cámbialo.*
yourTurn.answer: Si Vale quiere cambiar el menú, que lo cambie.
yourTurn.why: About a third person, the command becomes *que* + the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Speak to a friend (*tú*): *Si quiere llamarla, que la llame.*
yourTurn.why: To the person, drop *que* and use the plain command.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *que* the verb takes its wish form: *vaya*, not *va*.
Almost. To the person in front of you, use the plain command; *que* is for someone else.

pitfalls.wrong: Si quiere decírselo, que diga se lo.
pitfalls.right: Si quiere decírselo, que se lo diga.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The pronouns go before the verb: *que se lo diga*.

personal: Think of a small decision a friend keeps asking you about, and give them the green light with *Si quieres…*.
